Formaldehyde (PFA) alone can leave the chromatin “sticky”: proteins that are not truly bound to DNA at a given locus (including the antibody’s target protein or the antibody itself) can be trapped nonspecifically at regions of very open, highly transcribed chromatin. Those regions are precisely active promoters and enhancers (“hyper-ChIP-able” or “HOT” regions) that are rich in RNA-pol II, Mediator, histone acetylation, etc. When a second, protein-protein cross-linker such as DSG is added before PFA, it tends to fix protein complexes in place and reduces this artifactual trapping, so these spurious peaks disappear. Therefore, the peaks present with PFA alone but lost with DSG + PFA are most likely the nonspecific “hyper-ChIP-able” peaks at active regulatory elements.

Answer: D
